title: Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection
summary: The paper introduces token-level text anomaly detection and argues that existing methods are either document-level or narrowly task-specific. It proposes TokenCore, which uses BERT-base-uncased embeddings, max-pools subword embeddings to word level, builds a memory bank of normal token embeddings, and scores tokens by nearest-neighbor distance with mean aggregation for documents. On three token-annotated datasets, TokenCore achieves the best average AUROC at both token (0.7145) and document (0.7335) levels, though it is not best on SMS_Spam token-level.

match_target.why: The hint targets TokenCore token-level Grammar AUROC. The supplied excerpt shows 0.6371 in Table 1's token-level TokenCore row, Grammar ROC column (the hint calls this Table 3). This is the cheapest central single-dataset result: one BERT-base inference pass and exact nearest-neighbor scoring over 300 short Grammar sentences.

tolerance.why: Rule 3: AUROC is a bounded score, the paper prints it in [0,1], and the Grammar dataset has only 300 documents (<2,000). The paper reports no std for this value, so use 0.02 absolute.

requirements.quote: All the methods operate on BERT-base-uncased embeddings with max pooling aggregation.

requirements.stmt: Aggregate subword embeddings to word-level embeddings with element-wise max pooling.
requirements.quote: where the max operation is applied element-wise across each embedding dimension.

requirements.stmt: Build the memory bank from all normal training tokens only.
requirements.quote: we extract word-level embeddings from all normal samples in the training set and store them in a memory bank

requirements.stmt: Score each test token by its minimum distance to a memory-bank token.
requirements.quote: we compute its anomaly score as the distance to its nearest neighbor in the memory bank

requirements.stmt: Aggregate token scores into a document score by mean pooling.
requirements.quote: we aggregate token-level scores across all tokens in the document. We use mean aggregation

requirements.stmt: Use 50% of normal documents for the memory bank and the rest plus anomalies for testing.
requirements.quote: We use 50% normal documents as training data, the rest of data are set as testing including both normal and anomaly.
We compare TokenCore against 6 anomaly detection methods and use AUROC and AUPRC as evaluation metrics.

requirements.stmt: Align subword embeddings to word-level token annotations.
requirements.quote: we need to aggregate subword embeddings to obtain word-level representations for alignment with token-level annotations.

requirements.stmt: Use nearest-normal-neighbor distance as the anomaly criterion.
requirements.quote: construct a memory bank of normal token embeddings and measure anomalies based on distance to the nearest normal neighbor.

requirements.stmt: Construct the Grammar evaluation set from 270 correct and 30 incorrect sentences.
requirements.quote: selecting 270 correct sentences as normal samples and 30 incorrect sentences as anomalous samples

requirements.stmt: Use the SMS Spam dataset with 393 anomalous documents out of 4518.
requirements.quote: This dataset has 393 anomalous samples in total 4518 documents, anomaly rate is 8.7%.

requirements.stmt: Use the Restaurant Review dataset with 50 anomalous documents out of 1100.
requirements.quote: This dataset has 50 anomalous samples in total 1100 documents, anomaly rate is 4.5%.

requirements.stmt: Annotate negative-sentiment words or phrases as Review token anomalies.
requirements.quote: For token-level annotation, we identify and mark specific words or phrases that convey strong negative sentiment

requirements.stmt: Inject meaningless character sequences into normal SMS messages as anomalies.
requirements.quote: we randomly select portions of normal messages and inject meaningless character sequences such as ‘jasdhnjsdb’
